Pass or fail gate (GAP-0447): all six criteria, AC1 to AC6, pass on the stubs and again on the real owners. The environment, base hosts, fixture layout, extract format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0447) and are fixed at the wave 4 entry check with the data steward. The SCR-45 route path and the break-list fields are taken from the gateway-bff contract once published. Until the rwb-source-data and rwb-case contracts publish the reconciliation, key-resolution and freshness reads, the harness pins the operation and the shape it uses and fails the hop on a mismatch (GAP-0441).

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A break, an orphan or a stale product never deletes or changes a Workbench record or an ACE row; the console is read only and the harness writes nothing | Legacy RWB-AD-019 guardrails; AC2 |
| BR2 | The REC-01 to REC-05 rows are read as the JOB-04 reconciliation of rwb-source-data produced them, and the variance and the variance percent are never recomputed at the screen or in the harness | Legacy AC1; Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-04 owner rwb-source-data); MSG-P1-012 |
| BR3 | A break row carries the product group, the business date, the source count, the workbench count, the variance and the variance percent, and the account keys on the break with their days past due | Legacy AC1; `reconciliation_result` (DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129) |
| BR4 | A business key held on a case table with no row in the source contract is listed with its table, its column and its key, and the case and its row are unchanged | Legacy AC2; REC-05 |
| BR5 | The referential check covers the keys rwb-case itself holds: `case_party.person_key`, `case_account.account_key` and `recovery_case.primary_person_key`; it reads no other service's table | DP-05; Ownership Map rows `case_party`, `case_account`, `recovery_case` all P3 |
| BR6 | A data product is stale when the ACE batch for its expected business date is not complete, and it is shown with its last complete ACE business date and MSG-P1-001 | Legacy AC3; `data_product_load` (DF-OPS-001 to DF-OPS-008); MSG-P1-001 |
| BR7 | Freshness is read through the rwb-source-data freshness operation; no service reads `data_product_load` by table and no service reads an ACE view but rwb-source-data | DP-05; ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 41 (P1 owns freshness) |
| BR8 | A break row shows the case number, the queue and the owner of a key from schema `rwb_case` only, and shows the key alone when no case holds it | DP-05; AC1; Ownership Map rows `recovery_case` and `case_account` P3, `case_list_row` P1 |
| BR9 | The stale set is refreshed by a Temporal Schedule in rwb-case through the workflow kit; no Quartz job table and no shared job table is read, because JOB-05 is retired and the Schedules belong to each service | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-05 durable timers, retired) |
| BR10 | SCR-45 is served by a gateway-bff composite route that composes the three reads in parallel, one hop each, and never a page that calls four services itself | DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 44 note |
| BR11 | Every call is one REST hop on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget and a circuit breaker per downstream, never an in-process call and never a second hop | ADR-020; DP-11; DP-13 |
| BR12 | A product whose freshness is unknown is never shown as fresh; a stale block that has not been refreshed shows the business date of its last refresh and nothing else | BR6; Legacy AC3 pattern |
